# Appeal of Denial — Partial Knee Replacement (CPT 27446)

**Member:** Riley Grant
**Member ID:** W485404613
**Payer/Plan:** CountyCare (Commercial/ACA), Illinois
**Denial date:** 2026-08-09
**Reference number:** POC-5767D9118E-71989
**Governing policy:** EVH CG 2734.CC Outpatient Major Joint Arthroplasty (Hips and Knees), effective 2026-01-01 — https://countycare.com/wp-content/uploads/ECG_2734.CC-for-Outpatient-Major-Joint-Arthroplasy-Hips-and-Knees-ver-Dec-25.pdf

Dear CountyCare Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my request for a partial knee replacement (CPT 27446), which was denied on 2026-08-09 with the stated reason that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." My surgeon, Dr. Marchetti, has documented that this procedure is needed, and I am asking CountyCare to reconsider this decision using its own published criteria.

## Why I believe the criteria are met

The plan's policy, EVH CG 2734.CC, states:

> "Replacement/revision of previous arthroplasty Replacement/revision TKA or THA may be considered necessary as an inpatient procedure when the following criteria are met:"

> "● Effusions ● Acute fracture ● Avascular necrosis ● Joint space narrowing or large osteophytes on imaging ● Severe sclerosis or deformity ● Bone on bone contact WITH At least 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment documented in the medical record (6,16,17):"

My medical records show:

- **Imaging:** An MRI of the knee dated 2026-05-30 documented "full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition" and "Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 medially." This directly corresponds to two of the imaging findings the plan's own policy lists — "joint space narrowing or large osteophytes on imaging" and "bone on bone contact."

- **Non-surgical treatment:** My records document more than 12 weeks of non-surgical treatment. I completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (18 visits, 2026-05-15 to 2026-07-10), documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-19 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. My symptoms have been present and progressive for 9 months. Taken together, this treatment history spans well beyond the 12-week period the policy references.

- **Functional impact:** My records also document that I cannot climb stairs without assistance and wake 3-4 times nightly with pain, along with positive provocative testing and range of motion limited by pain on exam.

The policy also states that "[w]here a specific clinical indication is not directly addressed in this guideline, medical necessity determination will be made based on widely accepted standard of care criteria," and that the guideline's criteria "were developed utilizing evidence-based and peer-reviewed resources from medical publications and societal organization guidelines as well as from widely accepted standard of care, best practice recommendations." I ask that my surgeon's documentation be evaluated against that same standard.

I note that the policy also references "LIMITATIONS FOR OUTPATIENT TKA OR THA" that "deems outpatient TKA or THA as not appropriate," but the specific limiting criteria were not included in the denial notice or the excerpts provided to me. If this section is part of the basis for the denial, I ask that CountyCare identify which specific limitation applies to my case so that I can address it directly.

## What I am asking for

I am asking CountyCare to reverse this denial and approve the partial knee replacement (CPT 27446) recommended by my surgeon, based on the imaging and treatment history documented in my medical record and summarized above.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-02-05. Please let me know if you need any additional records from Dr. Marchetti's office to complete this review.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Riley Grant
Member ID: W485404613
Date: [DATE OF SIGNATURE]
Contact phone: [PHONE NUMBER]
Contact address: [MAILING ADDRESS]

**Submission:** Please send this appeal to the appeal address printed on your denial letter, or call the number on the back of your insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.

**Enclosures:** [Copy of denial notice, physical therapy discharge note, MRI report dated 2026-05-30, surgeon's letter of medical necessity — attach as applicable]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
